claim: The original claim that CAS INSERT survives an object-store fault while CAS MERGE reruns the whole merge was refuted: both operations fail with the same CAS `Code 236 ABORTED` when the mount lease is lost.

A sustained object-store fault can fail the mount-lease renewal PUT, let the lease deadline expire, trip the write fence, and cause every subsequent write to reject at `stageManifest` before attempting a write until self-remount recovers.

The mount-lease protocol is fail-closed: another writer cannot claim a slot until the current lease expires, so continuing to write while `now < lease_deadline` is safe unless a proven supersession has occurred.

`SingleWriterSlot::backgroundLoop` treats any exception from `renewOnce` as terminal, while `renewOnce` can throw from `putOverwrite` before checking the returned token; a transient network fault is therefore misread as foreign-token supersession and burns the writer incarnation.

The existing replicated-merge exponential backoff is defeated when CAS uses `ABORTED`: `ReplicatedMergeMutateTaskBase` treats `ABORTED` as deliberate cancellation, so `last_exception_time_ms` remains zero and a failed merge can be recomputed in a tight loop.

CAS retry-later failures were opaque because the message said `retry budget exhausted` even for a pre-attempt fence rejection, and the failures were logged at Information level without populating `system.replication_queue.last_exception`.

Fix #37 distinguishes a confirmed token mismatch from a transient renewal exception: a completed PUT returning a foreign owner or epoch fences immediately, while a thrown `putOverwrite` is retried while the confirmed lease remains outside its safety margin.

The fail-close boundary for renewal is the lease deadline, with `now + lease_safety_margin >= lease_deadline` causing a fence when no successful renewal has refreshed the deadline; a proven supersession still fences immediately.
The renewal fix is confined to `CasServerRoot` and `MountLeaseKeeper`; it does not change generic or upstream ClickHouse code.
Escaping CAS retry-later failures are routed through `throwCasWriteRetryLater`, which throws `Exception(ErrorCodes::NETWORK_ERROR, "CAS write could not be committed ({}); retrying later", why)`.

`NETWORK_ERROR` was chosen for CAS retry-later failures because it is outside the merge exemption set, participates in ClickHouse's transient retry taxonomy, and does not receive conflicting special handling on the CAS commit path.

If `NETWORK_ERROR` later proves too coarse, the documented escape hatch is a dedicated `CONTENT_ADDRESSED_WRITE_RETRY_LATER` error code, with optional additions to `checkDataPart::isRetryableException` and HTTP mapping.

The retry-later helper covers the escaping retry-later throws in `CasPartWriteTxn.cpp` and `CasRefLedger.cpp`, while internal `ABORTED` control-flow signals, startup/decommission failures, live-lock brakes, genuine content conflicts, and GC-internal values retain `ABORTED`.

After `uploadFromSource` maps an unresolved conditional create to `NETWORK_ERROR`, `putBlob` no longer retries that fence-lost or unresolved case eight times locally; it escapes to merge-level backoff on the first outer attempt.

The retry-later helper's message carries the precise cause, and changing the escaping error to non-exempt `NETWORK_ERROR` automatically populates `system.replication_queue.last_exception` and `last_exception_time` through existing merge handling.

The planned S3-fault regression has a short-fault leg below lease TTL that must preserve the lease and a long-fault leg above lease TTL that must fence, back off, recover, and finish with `fsck` reporting `dangling=0`.

Preserving staged merged parts or implementing resume-upload is explicitly out of scope because content-addressed blob deduplication bounds recompute cost once lease renewal stops over-fencing and merge backoff engages.
A new dedicated error code and MOVE-to-CA support are separate non-goals of the merge upload-retry fix; the former is only a documented escape hatch and the latter has its own design.

The implementation plan adds `SingleWriterSlot::shouldFenceOnTransientRenewFailure()` as a protected virtual hook defaulting to `true`, with `MountLeaseKeeper` overriding it for deadline-aware retry behavior.
`MountLeaseKeeper` refreshes its confirmed lease deadline on both successful `claim` paths and every successful background renewal.
The new `MountLeaseKeeper` `lease_safety_margin_` constructor parameter is appended after the existing `event_sink_` parameter and has a default of 2000 milliseconds, preserving existing call sites.
Production `CasMountRuntime::installKeeper` passes `cas_request_budget.lease_safety_margin_ms` to `MountLeaseKeeper`.

The retry-later API has both `throwCasWriteRetryLater(const String & why)` and `makeCasWriteRetryLaterExceptionPtr(const String & why)`, and both carry `ErrorCodes::NETWORK_ERROR` with the same message shape.
The planned retry-later warning uses `LogSeriesLimiter` with one allowed message per 30-second interval and logs at Warning level under the logger name `CasWriteRetryLater`.
The permanent S39 regression is intended to exercise a degraded-but-alive object store, because prior chaos coverage faulted nodes but not S3 while nodes remained alive.
S39's long-fault assertions require a populated `system.replication_queue.last_exception` and successful post-recovery writes before running an `fsck`-to-fixpoint check.
The source-layout refactor target tree is `Primitives → Formats → Backend → Pool → Gc → Tools ≈ Parts → facade`.

The source-layout refactor's include-direction rule permits a file to include only its own layer and layers to its left, with named exceptions for the staging sweeper and `probeConditionalCopy` bypassing `Backend` into `IObjectStorage` and for `Backend` reading `Formats` traits.

The source-layout refactor preserves behavior by forbidding mutex coverage or lock-order changes, construction/destruction-order changes, persisted-byte/key changes, log/event/metric changes, and mixing file moves with content edits in one commit.

Renaming `Store` to `Pool` and `Build` to `PartWriteTxn` changes only C++ identifiers and file names; the protocol vocabulary `build_seq`, `buildSeq`, `BuildPrefix`, upload stamps, and related build-sequence identifiers remains unchanged.

The identity micro-header merge places `RootNamespace`, `Token`, `BlobDigest`, `BlobRef`, `ManifestId`, and `RefTxnId` in `CasTypes.h`, while codec and hex helpers remain in the separate `CasCodecUtil.h` file.
`CasRefProtocol` contains the ref replay and intake planning logic, while the two ref codecs remain in `Formats/` and are not pulled into the protocol component.

`CasStore` decomposition is defined by state and lock ownership: each extracted component moves its guarded state and mutexes wholesale, receives environment through constructor parameters or callbacks, and must not retain a `Pool &` back-reference.
`CasPlainObjects` is stateless over `Backend &` and `const Layout &`, and `CasStore` retains the external API through thin delegates.
`CasManifestReader` owns manifest reads, the token-gated byte-weighted decode cache, its LRU, and the cache mutex, while `CasStore` delegates the read API to it.

`CasRefLedger` owns the ref-table map, ref-queue and per-table state mutexes, append/recovery/seal lanes, snapshot publication, stale-precommit sweep, cache eviction, remount coordination, and ref lifecycle/read entry points.

`CasMountRuntime` owns mount fencing, the mount lease keeper, self-remount machinery, and build-sequence watermarks, while `CasStore` retains the `open` and `tryRemountOnce` orchestration and its claim→ledger-quiesce→fence-rearm order.

The proposed `CasBlobUploader` extraction moves byte delivery such as `putBlob`, `observeAndAdmit`, `uploadFromSource`, HEAD-first handling, and staging promote/resurrect execution, while admit/adopt/resurrect choice, dependency recording, and the `promote` gate remain transaction state.

The post-v3 source inventory explicitly keeps `CasCodecUtil.h` as a separate `Primitives` utility, places `CasSourceEdgeMarkers.h` in `Primitives`, moves `CasWireVocab` and `CasRefWireVocab` with `Formats`, realizes `CasPoolMeta` as `Pool/CasPoolMeta.cpp` only, and places `CasInspect` in `Tools`.

The CA CMake setup requires explicit `add_headers_and_sources` entries for `Primitives`, `Formats`, `Backend`, `Pool`, `Gc`, `Tools`, and `Parts` because the directory glob is non-recursive; gtests are discovered recursively and need no test-CMake edit.

The codecs-v3 migration exposed a cross-translation-unit ODR violation because old and new implementations defined identical `DB::Cas` codec functions; the safe resolution was an atomic cutover deleting `CasManifestCodec.{h,cpp}` before trusted shape tests.
The codecs-v3 audit concluded that all 15 live persisted CAS objects have text codecs under `Core/Formats/`, no `.proto` files remain, and both binary codecs were deleted.
The codecs-v3 phase-3 soak completed with `dangling=0`, equal oracle counts on both replicas, recovered from four faults and two restarts, and drained the pool from about 3 GB to 102 MB.
The apparent codecs-v3 `CANNOT_PARSE_INPUT_ASSERTION_FAILED` and `S3_ERROR` increases were classified as expected workload SQL parser fallback and write-once dedup races, not codec regressions.
The codecs-v3 soak's dominant `S3HeadObject` activity and one fsck timeout were attributed to pre-existing B146/B154 fold and GC blob-existence probing, not to `.zst` parsing or codec CPU overhead.
The source-layout mechanical phase created the layered tree, completed eight merges, moved 107 files to 89, and reached a green CA battery of 905 tests before hand C++ decomposition.

A CA soak identified `__copy_construct_tree` over `std::map<string,Cas::RefCommittedRow>` as the top CPU stack for ref-table commit operations; it was treated as a pre-existing scalability smell and backlogged rather than a correctness defect.

The proposed `CasBlobUploader` split was descoped because `putBlob`, `observeAndAdmit`, and `uploadFromSource` form one mutually recursive writer-protocol lane whose decision state is coupled to byte delivery and shared mid-flight state.

The source-layout rename verification required the counts of `build_seq`, `buildSeq`, `BuildPrefix`, `allocateBuildSeq`, `active_build_seqs`, `next_build_seq`, and `inflight_builds` to remain unchanged across the `Build`→`PartWriteTxn` rename.

MOVE PART or MOVE PARTITION to a CA disk was architecturally unimplemented: `PartPathParser::findPartDirComponent` had no `MergeTreeData::MOVING_DIR_NAME` case, so files under `moving` resolved to the same literal ref `moving`.

The deeper MOVE-to-CA failure was that non-zero-copy `clonePart` used per-file `copyFile` with a fresh autocommit transaction for each file, so a whole part could not publish as one CAS manifest and the second file collided on ref `moving`.
The proposed MOVE-to-CA fix is a CAS-aware `clonePart` path that stages the whole part in one `ContentAddressedTransaction`; the generic per-file cross-disk copy path is insufficient.

Scenario S37 passed 22 of 23 verdicts; all non-MOVE multi-disk legs passed, including policy placement, insert-time `max_data_part_size` routing, truthful `disk_name`, restart re-attach, and mixed-disk merge, while only cross-disk `clonePart` to CA failed.

The one-pipeline transaction design gives each CA disk transaction one mutable transaction-private overlay updated at call time, makes every transaction-scoped read observe it, and reserves durable publication for disk `commit`.

The one-pipeline design adds no `IDiskTransaction::precommit`, `IMetadataTransaction::precommit`, or `IDataPartStorage::publishStagedData`, and does not change `IDataPartStorage::precommitTransaction` or the Replicated `Keeper` call sequence.

The only permitted shared-code changes in the one-pipeline design are `transactionIsStagingOverlay()`, `tryCreateWriteBuffer(...)`, the generic `dispatch()` funnel, and a release-build assertion that eager transactions leave `operations_to_execute` empty.

The failpoint `disk_object_storage_fail_commit_metadata_transaction` throws inside `DiskObjectStorageTransaction::commit()` before `metadata_transaction->commit()`, after the Replicated `Keeper` multi has returned `ZOK`; this tests recovery from a part present in the Keeper part set but absent on disk.

When a post-`Keeper`-multi disk commit fails, ordinary recovery may enqueue the missing part for replica fetch or call `createEmptyPartInsteadOfLost` with `lost_part_count` incremented; the CA design adds no CA-specific recovery mechanism.

A failed repoint of an existing ref must not drop that ref during compensation: `publishStaging` returns false for the repoint path, so the ref is absent from `created_refs` and is not rolled back as newly created.

The B183 text-index scratch ref is published by a separate nested sub-storage and must still be dropped during staged-source `tmp`→final finalization even after the main transaction's publication moves to `commit`.

DDL committed-ref drops, moves, and RENAME TABLE operations are gated for explicit design-owner confirmation because deferring them to commit requires a `pending_ref_ops` overlay and new read-path behavior; the motivation bugs are in the part-build path.

The empty-covering-part `commitTransaction()` workaround must remain: the rollback path does not enter `MergeTreeData::Transaction::commit`, so that call is the only publication point for the empty cover under a commit-only publication design.
Whole-part atomicity sites such as `freeze`, restore-from-backup, and B58 projection commits remain single-`commit` transactions because this design deliberately introduces no `precommit` phase.

Verbatim table-level and mountpoint files are treated as an immediate autocommit class: writes are durable on finalize and deletes or moves remain durable at call time, avoiding a second timeline for those files.

The generic `tryCreateWriteBuffer` hook receives the owning `std::shared_ptr<IDiskTransaction>` so CA can keep the disk transaction alive for the buffer lifetime and commit from an autocommit finalize callback.
For a staging-overlay storage, `dispatch(op)` invokes `op(metadata_transaction)` immediately; for ordinary object storage it appends the operation to `operations_to_execute` for FIFO replay.
The release-build eager-transaction guard throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` before publication if `transactionIsStagingOverlay()` is true while `operations_to_execute` is non-empty.

The 02941 projection failure was caused by `tryGetInFlightFileSize` and `tryGetInFlightStorageObjects` returning `blob_size` for an Inline entry, even though manifest decoding leaves Inline `blob_size` at zero and stores the real size in `inline_bytes`.

The durable fix for the Inline-size bug was to return `inline_bytes.size()` for Inline entries, add the regression test `CaTransactionLockScope.InFlightReadCarriedForwardProjectionSidecar`, and preserve `blob_size` for Blob entries.

The later hardening added canonical `ManifestEntry::size()` and routed all size consumers through it, eliminating duplicated Inline-versus-Blob size ternaries while retaining legitimate Blob-object byte sites.
The TXN-final phase-3 soak completed with `dangling=0`, recovered from five faults and three restarts, reported `ABORTED-retried INSERT=0`, and drained the pool to 256 bytes.

The CA in-commit upload-retry stack is caller-agnostic: INSERT and MERGE share `putBlob`, `uploadFromSource`, and `CasRequestController`, and both keep the staged scratch temporary alive across retries.

When a MERGE exception escapes `commit()`, orchestration cancels and releases the task, `ContentAddressedTransaction` removes the staging key, and the replication scheduler later selects and recomputes the whole merge; INSERT instead surfaces the failure to its query caller.

`CasRequestControl` uses a 16-attempt, 90-second default operation budget, while `putBlob` has an outer eight-round loop that catches only `ABORTED`; deterministic local failures are rethrown immediately.

The S3-fault reproduction showed a mount-lease renewal PUT failing with `Code 499`, the write fence becoming lost pool-wide, self-remount being blocked for the fault duration, and recovery succeeding about 16 seconds after disarm without data loss or orphans.

In the same reproduction, plain INSERT failed with the byte-identical `Code 236 ABORTED` as MERGE; the observed difference was that MERGE was re-queued by replication and recomputed about every two seconds while INSERT surfaced the error to the client.

The tight merge loop was not caused by an absent queue backoff: `ReplicatedMergeTreeQueue::getPostponeTimeMsForEntry` already computes exponential backoff, but CAS `ABORTED` is exempted from `updateLastExeption`, leaving `last_exception_time_ms=0` and the computed postpone at zero.

Two independent consults validated three complementary CAS-side defects for #37: over-fencing on transient renewal errors, `ABORTED` defeating merge backoff, and opaque retry-later observability; they found no data-loss or recovery-wedge defect.

The #37 design selected existing `NETWORK_ERROR` through one `throwCasWriteRetryLater` helper, renewed while the lease deadline remained valid, and added an honest rate-limited Warning plus an S3-fault regression and fsck verification.

The #37 reproduction's reported no-orphan outcome was counter-supported but not fsck-verified; the follow-up requires running `fsck` to fixpoint after fence-loss recovery and relating the precommit-window edge to S30 `DANGLING-PRECOMMIT`.

The MOVE-to-CA design was reframed as one whole-part `ContentAddressedTransaction` threaded through the move, plus a layer-1 parser fix so the final part identity is used instead of `moving`; the earlier claim that a transactional copy would lack full build semantics was rejected.

The ref-table-copy performance investigation identified three candidate mechanisms for reducing `flushRefBatch` copying from whole-map cost to touched-row cost: a persistent immutable map, an overlay/delta over a shared base, and a copy-on-write wrapper over `std::map`.
The B199 recovery test fixture produced a foreign seal by appending `_FOREIGN_DIFFERENT` to valid seal bytes; after the formats-v3 cutover, that byte sequence is no longer a valid seal object.
After `cas_ref_snap` switched to zstd-framed text, appending garbage to a zstd frame causes one-shot decompression to fail with `Src size is incorrect`.
Recovery correctly fails closed when a foreign seal object is undecodable; the zstd frame check closed the earlier F3-1a decode-laxity finding rather than introducing a product bug.
The B199 test fix adds `RefWriterTestBackend::corrupt_foreign_bytes`, allowing tests to supply a valid foreign object or deliberate garbage instead of always appending garbage to valid bytes.

The corrected seal-conflict test constructs a valid foreign seal with the same namespace and seal id `(2, MAX)`, `sealed_from = (2,1)`, and three committed rows, then proves adoption with `listRefs().size() == 3`.

The corrected B199 validation passed all nine `RefWriterRecoverySeal.*` tests and the full selected Ca* battery with 907 tests run, 907 passed, and zero failures; two tests were pre-existing disabled tests.
The F3-1a adoption-of-a-corrupt-seal tolerance finding is moot after formats v3 because an undecodable foreign seal now fails recovery closed via the zstd frame check.
